rationale: Phase 1 blast-radius code meets F2/F6/F7/F8/F9 and keeps ingest 204 plus flag default False. No blocking production-readiness defect in the listed files. Concerns: integration/soak unrun; F9 is operator-invoked and can skip hot sites without a yield marker; Python utcnow() vs Postgres now() clock skew.
nonBlockingFindings: F9 run_aggregation_watermark_bootstrap is not registered in start_scheduler (intentional vs 24 add_job AST gate). Operator must invoke it and re-run until every site with events has last_aggregated_at. Hot sites can be skipped: F9 waits TTL+5 then returns contended and does not set the sweep yield marker.
Integration tests (test_visitor_aggregation_incremental, test_aggregation_debounce, test_aggregation_watermark_bootstrap) did not run: localhost:5433 and :6379 not listening.
Prod soak canary and Railway AGGREGATION_INCREMENTAL_ENABLED=true are operator leftovers, not proven by this review.

F2 writes Event.created_at = datetime.utcnow() (API process clock). Watermark stamps use SELECT now() (Postgres timestamptz, then _strip_tz). Small skew can drop events from the incremental window until the hourly full SET sweep.

RunLock leftover cooldown after a short run preserves flag-OFF debounce tests. This is compatible with F8 (mutex held during the run via refresh). After a run longer than TTL, cooldown is 0 so the next ingest may fire immediately.
F2 unit coverage is structural (source string). Behavioral proof lives in TestFutureEventTs, which is integration-gated and unrun.
notes: High-risk pack classes (auth/billing/schema/public-API/deploy/trust-boundary) are not in this blast radius. Pixel ingest 204 happy-path is unchanged. adversarial-validation.json is not required. Flip the Railway flag only after F9 reports no remaining NULL watermarks on sites that have events.
